So.

Yeah.

Yeah, sure.
Yeah.

Yeah, perfect.

So.
Yeah.
So, yeah, we are a capital A group and we're an M and A advisory.

So all of our clients are either on the buy or the sell side are buying and selling marketing agencies.
And we own and operate agencies code, which is the marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell agencies.
In the last 12 months, we've helped agencies buy and sell over and done over $100 million in transactions.
And we.
We've got a network of 130,000 buyers and sellers of marketing agencies.
So we work on a global.
Sort of on a global scale, but I would say probably about 90% of our business is in the U.S. okay.
So today my role really is just to find out as much as can about what you guys are thinking.
Yeah.
We can go through how we can help you with our sell side process.
That sounds good.
That's great.
Yeah, no, that.
That's really helpful.
And yeah, we can tell you a little bit about us and.
And a little bit about what, what we're thinking.
Yeah.
At a really high level.
Ryan and I have worked together for a really long time.
We came from a bigger company where we broke 2017 and started Interecho.

We do it end to end for them.
So we start on that upstream.

You know, we're working with, with, with native video assets, recutting video, doing voiceover work.
Sometimes clients come to us.
There is no English master.
We need to create original content for Germany or Japan or wherever it may be.
We have the production capabilities to do that as well.
So we do act as a little bit of a production house in a smaller capacity.
So we, we've just started thinking about our exit strategy and like what our thinking is, is that we ultimately we're not ready to exit the business per se.

We would love to join a larger ecosystem of potential agencies or maybe it's, you know, larger localization company, something where we can fold in and be a complementary element to what they're doing.
We see it as a potential business development strategy for us.
Maybe we get a little bit of cash out of the business.
You know, we take equity on the, on the other side of the buyer and then we stay on for five, five years or more, you know, kind of a thing.

Yeah.
Okay, cool.
Thank you for that.
So.
So the, the agency is owned by just the two of you?
Yes.

Yeah.
Okay, and how dependent is the business on both of you?

Yeah, yeah, yeah, absolutely.
Yeah.

So.

Yeah.
Okay, and so your revenue numbers, you're, you're doing what, two.
Was it two million?
Yeah.
Okay.
Ebitda.
Yeah, yeah, a little over two million.
You know, that'll be top line.
Top line.
Revenue this year will be a little over two, two and a half.
EBITDA is going to be.
Well, it's going to have to be adjusted because like we're an S corporation.
We, we definitely utilize the business a little bit for ourselves.
You know, we run a lot through the company just from a tax, you know, standpoint.
We're, we're an S corp.
So we're set up to take, Ryan and I are both on a small salary and then we take distributions on profit.
But yeah, a little over 2 million.
Top line.
Okay, brilliant.
And what is your ultimate sort of endpoint?
Obviously you want to stay in the business for the foreseeable future, but you're looking to basically sell and then do a reasonable earn out, get out.
Three years.
Yeah, I'd probably say five years.
I mean, I think that that's probably a reasonable target.
Certainly for me.
I'm a little bit older than Ryan.
But, you know, we've talked and I, you know, I think five years, you know, is, is what we're, is when we're looking to exit, we would definitely still want to continue to stay on.
And I don't know if that makes us more valuable or not.
You know, I mean, that's part of what we're looking at is finding that right kind of buyer, you know, that isn't looking just to acquire and, and, and, and exit us immediately.
Like, yeah, we would love, we would love to continue.
Yeah.
Actually the majority of buyers prefer the founders to stay in as long as possible, Usually a three to five year handover.
Okay.
Yeah.
Quite often founders just stay in the, in the larger business as, you know, maybe a board member or just in a leadership role.
Okay.
So, yeah, not usually a problem.
I would say there are sort of buyer operators that have got SBA loans that do want to buy out founders and take them out of the business.
But there's definitely the two different types of buyers there and we tend to have more of the more sort of institutionally backed buyers in our database.
So they tend to want to keep you in.
And so any issues in the business, I mean, what's the reason for coming to this point?
Why are we here today?
I think it's just long.
Like I personally want to be retired by 2032.
That's always been my number.
That's when my kids are kind of out in school, often doing their own thing.
I think that's it for me is like, how am I going to exit?
And so, I mean, that's the big push for me.
I think the other push for us too is based upon the fact that I see somewhat of a business development strategy for us.
We are growing, we are profitable.
But would it behoove us to.
To join a larger ecosystem that has clients that we complement their business?
They don't have necessarily the skill set that we have.
And are we able to get folded into a larger agency where we can bring real value and that just sustains us?
It becomes less about transactional business development growth year over year for us, and it becomes more about us doing what we really do well and doing that with an existing agency's client base.
I think those are the two things for me.
I mean, r. I don't know if you have anything to add to that.
Yeah, I mean, I think that pretty much covers it.
Yeah.
I mean that business development is a big part of it.
Right.
Like it's, it definitely like that.
It would be, it would be nice to be, have, have kind of.
Yeah, to be able to kind of focus on what we do well and still focus on business development, but have a little bit more of a pipeline coming in, essentially.
And do you, do you have a timeline at all, guys?
Are you just data gathering at the moment or is it like something that you're looking to pull the trigger on relatively?
Yeah, yeah.
No, I mean, we're Data gathering right now.

So that, that is stuff that we are in the process of building as we speak and it's going to be operational within Q1 of next year.
We think that adds value to our business.
I think we would want that to be all fleshed out before we ever, you know, sort of went to market with ourselves.
You know, I would say it's, it's, it's potentially a 20, 26 transaction for us.
Maybe middle of next year we really get into it and we start to market ourselves and put ourselves on the market.
So yeah, that's reasonable timeline for us.
I think it would probably be middle of next year would be, you know, probably the soonest that we would, we would want to do something.
So right now we're in that data gathering process.
And what's the tool that you're creating?
Why do you feel that it would add value to the business?
Yeah, I mean, it's specifically on the translation side and it's specifically utilizing.
I mean, there's a lot of AI translation out there today.
There's, you know, all the LLMs.
You can use Google Translate or OpenAI or whatever and utilize it to get translation done.
It's very literal.
It's very word for word.

What we're doing is we're building on top of those existing LLMs AI capabilities that can understand actual brand writing style, brand tone, pull glossaries of terminology specific to the brand that have been translated by humans in the past and teaching that technology and machine to be able to replicate that.
So it's a lot better than off the shelf AI translation.
It's going to be much more transcreation and culturally relevant specific.
So the machine itself is essentially going to replace a human copywriter that is doing that stuff right now at a very literal level.
So we see it as an advantage.
We have clients today that are asking us for that.
We see it too as an opportunity for us to become more profitable.
Because if we're able to utilize that technology on the front end of work and then we just have human proofreaders that are coming in and polishing the, the content.
Our costs go way down, you know, so it adds profitability potentially.
Is that something we pass on to clients to make our services cheaper?
Maybe, you know, I mean, I don't know where we're going to go with it.
But that's at a high level, that's what we're building.
And so would that tool be like a SaaS product where you have clients logging in at the front, people subscribing, or is it just an internal tool that gets your margins up?
Yeah, it's all on the table right now.
So potentially could potentially become a SaaS product.
I think it sort of depends on where we take it and what we can actually do with it from a capability standpoint.
Right.
Like, you know, right now we're thinking of it as a complement to our service, but maybe it becomes a SaaS product and it makes our valuation a lot higher if that suddenly becomes a big part of the.
Right like that.
I imagine that's why you're asking that from a, from a valuation.
I mean, as a tool, you're exactly right.
So as a, as a tool you use internally, you get bigger margins, you employ less people, you know is quicker, better, cheaper.
Whether you pass that saving on or whether that's better margin for you is one of those two things.
But that's bigger margins.
Multiples are still going to be the same.

Nobody's paying bigger multiples because you are using AI.
Everybody's using AI.
If you create a SaaS tool, that's something different.
Obviously a SaaS product is IP in and of itself.
If you are scaling, I mean, these things can't be done in a few months.
It maybe is a year or two years of, of building and scaling that before you create the value that you can exit with.
But certainly assess tools.
Multiples are different, IP is priced differently and you're looking more, you know, more either double digit multiples or single digit multiples of rather than ebitda.
So definitely, yeah, Hello.
Experienced or kind of tooled up to create those types of business structures and can end up being just a massive cost base for you.

So it depends, you know, people are kind of in the startup space or you know very much about product development and a software development are able to do that successfully and agency owners should definitely give it a try if they can do it easily.
But it is a different type of buyer, this different business model.
There's lots of service involved, there's lots of refunds.
I mean, it's just a completely different space to be in.
Okay.
It doesn't suit everybody, but yeah, certainly it's two different ways to value the business.
So from our point of view we can help you in a couple of different tiered service offerings that we have.
The top tier is probably a bit too excessive for where you're at at the moment.
We kind of run a full M and a process which costs $30,000.

And that's more really for founders that are looking to get out six months or less where they're creating a sort of process that generates interest and offers within a six month timeline, whereas we have a sort of standard process.
And it's not that it's any slower, it can be just as quick, if not even quicker, but there's kind of less real need for support from us.
What we're doing is helping you get to market.
So we're creating a valuation for the business.
We're setting up all of the marketing for you.
So creating your im, creating the teaser, creating the listing on our website.
And then really the main piece is creating a bespoke list of buyers and marketing to that list.
And we manage the whole process end to end.
But really it's kind of like a three or four week get ready for market and then a sort of one or two months sprint to get you in front of as many people as possible.
And then we have a sort of self service offering at two and a half thousand dollars.
Really you're just getting your own listing up on the site, but you have to build all of your own marketing tools and kind of guess your valuation a little bit.
But again, we find buyers and we do successfully find buyers very quickly because we have a subscriber list of 20,000 agency buyers and sellers and we've had like 45 signed NDAs in 24 hours.
And you know, a sales process running to two or three months to get people out that way.
So I mean it is successful, but it's just less hand holding for that.
So those are the kind of three different flavors that we do.
Okay.
Really?
Yeah, I mean it's down to what suits your needs.
Most people just pick the standard approach where we help them just get to market basically and then get it out to, to our marketplace.
But also building that bespoke list of buys is where the real value comes in.
So yeah, so I can put all of those options in an email for you guys.
What I would say is the process generally speaking runs to around six months, sometimes a bit quicker, sometimes a bit slower.
So if you were looking really to, to get out and exit before the end of next year, really I would say the end of Q1 is probably the time to go to market rather than the middle of the Year.
Okay.
Summer's a bit slow and then really don't have September, October and a bit of November to.
To kind of shake out.
Yeah, that's what I was going to ask you.
I was going to ask if.
If timing of the year comes into play on.
On this.

You know, is there.
Is there a sweet spot in terms of when businesses should really like, put themselves out there?
Yeah, there's a couple.
There's a couple of times a real busy periods.
I would say sort of second or third week in September is extremely busy.
October is.
Is really busy.

November, the start of Emery is good, but obviously we're going to Thanksgiving and things start to slow down at that point.
And if we do have buyers at the table, I mean, people aren't hanging up their spurs for the winter at all.
I mean, they will still continue to get a deal done.
But going to market in December is obviously not great.
And January is notoriously slow.
But again, things pick up.
February and March and are extremely busy into the sort of summer months.
But July, August, again, difficult people on holiday.
Yeah, just hard to get anything closed.
So, yeah, start, start the year is great.
I would say a good point for, for us certainly is December to do all the prep and then hit the market in mid to late January is a pretty good time.
But.
But I would say for your.
You guys, the timing that you're considering, I probably around Easter would be better than waiting until you get into the middle of the year.
Yeah, yeah, definitely.
Yeah.
To start the prep and whatnot.
Okay, that makes sense.
Yeah.
Okay, good.
All right, so I'll get everything ready in an email send over.
You've got it to.
To hand when you guys want to, you know, make the next steps.
I'll put something in the diary as well to follow up maybe mid February and see where you go.
Yeah, I think that's fair.
That's great.
Yeah, no, this is a great first step.
Thanks for taking the time.
Yeah.
Glad we found you guys.
And yeah, we'll look out for your email.
Yeah, no worries.
Brilliant.
Okay.
And if you're not on our mailing list, sign up to our mailing list.
You'll get a flavor of what.
What gets listed and you know that.
That sort of thing.
So definitely, definitely.
Great.
All right, have a great day.
Yeah, thank you.
We'll speak soon.
Thanks.
Andrew.
All right.

summary.overview:
- **Company Overview:** Founded in 2017, the agency has 8 employees and generated over $2 million in revenue this year.  
- **Exit Strategy:** Founders target a sale by 2026 with a 5-year earn-out to ensure a smooth transition.  
- **Tech Development:** Developing an AI localization tool by Q1 next year to improve quality and boost profitability.  
- **M&A Timing:** Recommended to initiate market prep by December; peak buyer interest occurs mid-September to November.  
- **Financial Health:** Profitable agency with no debt, stabilizing operational functions to attract institutional buyers.  
- **Market Differentiation:** Specializes in transcreation, leveraging AI for culturally relevant translations, enhancing appeal in competitive landscape.
summary.short_summary: The agency, founded in 2017 by Nick Koumaris and Ryan Okie, is a profitable localization and marketing services provider with 8 full-time employees and over $2 million in revenue this year. The founders aim to exit by 2026 with a sale and a 5-year earn-out, anticipating that joining a larger agency will enhance their growth potential. They are developing an AI localization tool to improve translation quality, which may evolve into a SaaS product, impacting their valuation. Andy Day presented various M&A service options and highlighted the importance of timing for market preparation, recommending a strategy to maximize buyer engagement. The agency specializes in transcreation, integrating localization into creative development to differentiate itself in a competitive market.
